title: 虞美人·听雨
titleEn: The Beautiful Lady Yu: Listening to the Rain
author: 蒋捷
intro: A whole life in three scenes, each one simply “listening to the rain”: as a carefree youth, as a wandering adult, and as an old man in a monastery. A short poem that feels like a long life.
analysis: 这首词用“听雨”串起人的一生，选了三个画面。少年时，在歌楼上听雨，红烛、罗帐，热闹又浪漫，雨声只是背景。中年时，在旅途的小船上听雨，江面宽阔，乌云低垂，一只失群的孤雁在西风里叫——这是漂泊和孤独。老年时，在寺庙的僧房下听雨，鬓角已经斑白。最后说：人生的悲欢离合，本来就是无情的，就让台阶前的雨一滴一滴下到天亮吧。三个场景，三种心情，同一种雨声，听的人却变了。这种把一生压缩在几个画面里的写法，非常有力。结尾看似平静、“不在乎”，其实是经历了太多以后的无奈。作者经历了宋朝灭亡，后半生漂泊隐居，词里也有国破家亡的影子。
analysisEn: This ci strings a whole life together with one repeated act: listening to the rain. It gives us three pictures. As a youth, he hears rain from a singing house — red candles, silk bed-curtains, everything warm and romantic; the rain is just background music. In middle age, he hears it on a boat far from home: a wide river, low clouds, and a lone wild goose, separated from its flock, crying in the west wind — a picture of drifting and loneliness. Now, old, he hears it under the eaves of a monk’s lodging, his temples already flecked with white. And the ending: joy and grief, meeting and parting — none of it cares about us. So let the rain on the steps drip on, drop by drop, until dawn. Three scenes, three moods; the rain sounds the same, but the listener has changed. Compressing a lifetime into a few snapshots gives the poem great force. The calm of the ending is not indifference but the weariness of someone who has lived through too much — Jiang Jie saw the Song dynasty fall and spent his later years wandering and in hiding.
background: Jiang Jie (c. 1245–c. 1305) passed the top civil examination in 1274, just before the Mongol conquest ended the Southern Song. He refused to serve the Yuan and lived out his life in retreat; this poem is usually read as looking back from old age.
pronunciation: 少年：少 shào。一任：一 yī（按本调标注，口语变调读 yí）。鬓 bìn。僧庐 sēng lú。

lines.py: shào nián tīng yǔ gē lóu shàng
lines.lit: As a youth, I listened to the rain up in the singing house;
lines.en: Young, I heard the rain from a singing-house upstairs,

lines.lit: red candles dim on the silk bed-curtains.
lines.en: red candlelight soft on silk curtains.

lines.py: zhuàng nián tīng yǔ kè zhōu zhōng
lines.lit: In my prime, I listened to the rain in a traveller’s boat;
lines.en: In my prime, I heard it from a boat far from home —

lines.py: jiāng kuò yún dī, duàn yàn jiào xī fēng
lines.lit: the river wide, the clouds low, a stray goose crying in the west wind.
lines.en: wide river, low clouds, a lost goose crying into the west wind.

lines.py: ér jīn tīng yǔ sēng lú xià
lines.lit: Now I listen to the rain beneath a monk’s hut;
lines.en: Now I hear it under a monastery’s eaves,

lines.lit: my temples are already speckled like stars.
lines.en: my hair already flecked with grey.

lines.py: bēi huān lí hé zǒng wú qíng
lines.lit: Sorrow and joy, parting and meeting — all are without feeling;
lines.en: Grief and joy, partings and meetings — none of them care.

lines.py: yī rèn jiē qián, diǎn dī dào tiān míng
lines.lit: let it be: before the steps, drop by drop, until daybreak.
lines.en: Let the rain on the steps drip on, drop by drop, till dawn.

words.en: a house of singing and entertainment

words.note: 现代汉语仍用，约三四十岁。

words.en: a boat one travels on far from home
a wild goose separated from its flock

words.note: 现代汉语说“如今”“现在”，书面语也说“而今”。
古义，形容头发花白；今天“星星”指天上的星。

words.en: sorrows and joys, partings and reunions
words.note: 今天仍是常用成语，指人生的种种经历。

words.en: to let it be; to leave it to
words.note: 现代汉语说“任凭”“随它去”。
现代汉语“点点滴滴”；医院“打点滴”也是这个词。

imagery.name: 雨
imagery.zh: 同一种雨声贯穿一生，听雨的心情却从欢乐变成漂泊、再变成苍凉。
imagery.en: The same rain runs through a whole life, but the listener’s mood shifts from pleasure to drifting to bleak calm.

imagery.name: 烛
imagery.zh: 红烛罗帐是少年时温暖、浪漫的生活。
imagery.en: Red candles and silk curtains are the warm, romantic life of youth.

imagery.name: 雁
imagery.zh: 失群的孤雁在西风中鸣叫，正是中年漂泊、孤独的自己。
imagery.en: The lost goose crying in the west wind is the poet himself in middle age, alone and drifting.

imagery.name: 白发
imagery.zh: “鬓已星星”，头发斑白，写出老之已至、一生将尽。
imagery.en: Temples flecked with white: old age has arrived and life is nearly over.
